issue_context.title: `distribution` field not retrieved correctly on the `settings/embedders` route
issue_context.body: **Describe the bug** I added the following embedder to my settings: ``` "default": { "source": "openAi", "model": "text-embedding-ada-002", "apiKey": "sk-wv<...>", "documentTemplate": "A movie titled '{{doc.title}}' whose description starts with '{{doc.overview|truncatewords: 20}}'", "distribution": { "mean": 0.7, "sigma": 0.3 } }, ``` When I GET the `settings` route, I retrieve the following (which is correct): ``` "default": { "source": "openAi", "model": "text-embedding-ada-002", "apiKey": "sk-wvXXXXXX...", "documentTemplate": "A movie titled '{{doc.title}}' whose description starts with '{{doc.overview|truncatewords: 20}}'", "distribution": { "mean": 0.7, "sigma": 0.3 } } ``` But when I GET the `settings/embedders` route, I retrieve the following: ``` "default": { "source": "openAi", "model": "text-embedding-ada-002", "apiKey": "sk-wvXXXXXX...", "documentTemplate": "A movie titled '{{doc.title}}' whose description starts with '{{doc.overview|truncatewords: 20}}'", "distribution": { "mean": 0.699999988079071, "sigma": 0.30000001192092896 } }, ``` As you can see, the `distribution` field doesn't match the one I sent **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Enable the `vectorStore` exp. feature 2. Add a new embedder as the one described above 3. Check the `distribution` field by getting both the `settings` and the `settings/embedders` route. See inconsistency. **Expected behavior** The `distribution` field retrieved on the `settings/embedders` route should match the one I sent, and the one that I'm getting on the `settings` route **Screenshots** **Meilisearch version:** v1.8.0-rc.0

review_comments: Ok, it seems that it was the only embedder not showing the key (apart from the user-provided embeddings, of course). Nice, catch!
What is the point of this new `WildcardSetting` struct?
Ho! Ok, to simplify the usage of it, I see. Like, always calling `serialize_with_wildcard` when required.

Not only, the issue of serialize_with is also that the serialization is bound to the struct containing the field and not the type of the field itself, which means that `serde_json::json!(struct)["field_name"]` gives a different output than `serde_json::json!(struct.field_name)` which is not convenient for our case where we can get the full struct or a part depending on which route you are calling.
